primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: CYP7A1 encodes cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, which catalyzes the initial and rate-controlling step of the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway from cholesterol. Loss of CYP7A1 reduces bile-acid production and cholesterol catabolism, promoting hepatic cholesterol accumulation, increased LDL cholesterol, and gallstone/atherosclerotic risk.
vignette: A 32-year-old man has severe hypercholesterolemia despite adherence to a statin. He developed cholesterol gallstones in his twenties, and his father had premature coronary artery disease. Liver testing shows markedly reduced bile-acid synthesis. Genetic analysis identifies a homozygous loss-of-function variant in CYP7A1.
lead: Which of the following metabolic reactions is most directly impaired in this patient?
correct: 7alpha-hydroxylation of cholesterol during the initial step of the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway
distractors: Conjugation of bilirubin with glucuronic acid in hepatocytes
Canalicular export of conjugated bilirubin through MRP2
Microsomal transfer of triglyceride onto nascent apolipoprotein B
Conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate during cholesterol synthesis
distractor_notes: UGT1A1-mediated bilirubin conjugation is unrelated to CYP7A1-dependent cholesterol catabolism.
MRP2 mediates canalicular bilirubin transport and is defective in Dubin-Johnson syndrome, not CYP7A1 deficiency.
MTTP is required for ApoB lipoprotein assembly and is defective in abetalipoproteinemia.
HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes cholesterol synthesis; CYP7A1 instead initiates cholesterol disposal through classic bile-acid synthesis.
key_expl: Cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase is encoded by CYP7A1 and catalyzes the first committed step of the classic bile-acid pathway. Deficiency decreases conversion of cholesterol to bile acids and reduces a major route of cholesterol elimination. Human CYP7A1 deficiency has been associated with high LDL cholesterol, deficient bile-acid excretion, premature gallstones, and premature vascular disease.
objective: Identify CYP7A1 as the enzyme initiating the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway by 7alpha-hydroxylating cholesterol.
